newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Press group urges Serbia to give up broadcaster.
newsitem.headline: Press group urges Serbia to give up broadcaster.

text.p: The International Press Institute (IPI) denounced Serbia's ruling Socialists on Friday for ordering the police occupation of a local broadcasting station and expressed concern over the detention of two cameramen.

Opposition protestors blocked roads into the central Serbian city of Kragujevac on Thursday after the Socialist Party (SPS), defeated in a local poll, refused to hand over the RTK radio and television station there.
"The International Press Institute strongly condemns the forceful occupation by Serb authorities of RTK," the Vienna-based association said in an open letter to President Slobodan Milosevic.
IPI, which groups editors and media bosses in over 90 countries, said it was also disturbed by the police detention of two Associated Press cameramen and the confiscation of their tapes.
"Members of the press, both domestic and international, must be permitted to carry out their profession without interference," IPI wrote.

"IPI views these incidents as yet more examples of SPS resistance to democratic reforms. We strongly urge you (Milosevic) to...relinquish control of the broadcasting station immediately and allow the media to operate without further interference," it concluded.
On Thursday the new Zajedno (Together) coalition government in Kragujevac demanded that police and new managers brought in from Belgrade leave the radio and television station.
The new city council issued a statement denouncing "the latest open provocation of republican authorities and forcible takeover of RTV Kragujevac by Serbian police".
